notes: None of the four fixed paths (Data.WorldGenSettings.seed, Data.RandomSeed, top-level RandomSeed, top-level WorldGenSettings.seed) match here. extractSeedString's last two candidates (line 1403-1404) call findInteger(named:in:), which recurses into every compound value depth-first (line 1462-1484) until it finds a key named exactly 'RandomSeed' anywhere in the tree, checked before falling further to a bare 'seed' key search. This fallback exists precisely because level.dat's exact nesting has drifted across Minecraft versions (java-real-modern-format-legacy-fields-absent shows a real level.dat where even this recursive search finds nothing, since the value moved to a string field) -- findInteger only ever matches integer-typed NBT values (via nbtInteger's empty-path base case, line 1443-1456), so it would not find a same-named string tag even if one existed.
